children: The proposed transaction will give Solar’s step-down subsidiary Solar SA Investments 100 per cent of Omnia’s issued ordinary shares

Shares of Solar Industries India fell nearly 9 per cent on Tuesday after the explosives maker announced a Rs 12,951 crore acquisition of South Africa-based Omnia Holdings, with investors weighing the size of the all-cash transaction against its potential strategic benefits.

The stock fell to around Rs 20,300 during morning trade, extending its decline from Monday’s close of Rs 22,290. The sharp fall came despite Goldman Sachs retaining its Buy rating and raising its target price to Rs 26,550, citing the potential benefits of the acquisition.

The proposed transaction, valued at around USD 1.355 billion, will give Solar’s step-down subsidiary Solar SA Investments 100 per cent of Omnia’s issued ordinary shares, excluding treasury shares. The offer is priced at ZAR 134.50 per share and remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
The transaction is expected to close in early to mid-2027. Omnia will subsequently be delisted from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and A2X Markets.

Goldman Sachs said the acquisition could strengthen Solar Industries’ position across the commercial explosives and blasting value chain, while providing access to new markets and a broader product portfolio.

The brokerage expects potential synergies between Omnia’s mining operations and Solar’s existing South African business. It also sees scope for Solar to expand in Australia and Indonesia and enter markets such as Canada and Brazil through Omnia’s distribution network.
Goldman has estimated potential FY28 earnings-per-share accretion of 11-25 per cent from the transaction and raised its target price to Rs 26,550 from Rs 20,180 while retaining its Buy rating.

The positive brokerage view contrasts with Tuesday’s market reaction, which indicates that investors are assessing the immediate financial and execution implications of a transaction equivalent to a significant portion of Solar Industries’ own market value.

Omnia operates across the mining and agriculture sectors and has a presence in more than 23 countries, with over 3,500 employees and around 70 distribution centres. It serves customers across 40 countries.
For the year ended March 31, Omnia reported revenue of around Rs 13,307 crore, or $1.41 billion.
Solar said the acquisition would expand its international presence and strengthen its position in commercial explosives and mining solutions.

The company has been pursuing overseas expansion alongside its existing explosives and defence businesses. The Omnia transaction would significantly increase its exposure to international mining markets and add agriculture-related products to its portfolio.

Solar Industries’ broader analyst view remains positive. Bloomberg data shows 15 of 18 analysts covering the stock have a Buy recommendation, two have a Hold and one has a Sell call. The 12-month consensus target of around Rs 22,401 implies limited upside from Friday’s closing price of Rs 22,290.

Following Tuesday’s decline, Solar Industries shares were down nearly 9 per cent at around Rs 20,300. Despite the fall, the stock remains up more than 67 per cent so far in 2026 and around 40 per cent over the past year.
